requests.title: Approve compiled package v4.1 as the implementation plan for November 7
requests.question: Approve requirements-compiled/v4.1 (on top of package v4, whose verification plan it uses unchanged) as the plan the event build follows: interface contracts, file ownership, state-machine tables, GitHub error matrix, Forma layout contract, verification execution plan and schedule?
options: A: approve v4.1, after v4 is approved (ODR-V4-01)
B: request changes
C: decline; build from v4 alone
requests.recommendation: A. v4.1 changes no requirement, obligation or test binding (preservation-report.json); it removes decisions the team would otherwise make inside the timed window.
requests.rationale: Only the owner approves a package (RDP-003). v4.1 depends on v4: approving v4.1 without v4 leaves the requirements unfrozen.
requests.impact: Until approved, v4.1 is a CANDIDATE. The event build may follow it as guidance but must report it unapproved.

requests.title: Confirm the reconciliation of FSHARP-TYPE-SHAPES sections 42 and 46
requests.question: At the owner's direction (2026-10-30), docs/FSHARP-TYPE-SHAPES.md §42 (persistence port with ProviderConflict) and §46 (module split with LocalStore.fs) now carry ADR-R7-001 supersession notes pointing to the v4.1 contracts and project structure, and docs/rehearsal-007/traceability.json lists both sections as superseded (the R7 persistence validator passes). Confirm?
options: A: confirm the reconciliation
B: request changes
requests.rationale: The edit follows the owner's instruction; the owner's record makes it authoritative.
requests.impact: With B, the notes are revised before v4.1 is approved.

requests.title: Accept the interface-first ordering changes of the v4.1 DAG
requests.question: v4.1 lets the interface freeze (T14) start before the kernel (T13) and the invariant tests (T12), and the save machine (T19) and GitHub provider (T20) start before the kernel, because the frozen contracts fix the types. It keeps the invariant tests before the save machine (T12 before T19, R4-01) and the kernel before integration checkpoint 1 (T13 before T17) and before live integration (T13 before T21). It also keeps the invariant tests before review checkpoint T35. The five v4 orderings it drops are listed with reasons in analysis/task-adjustments.json waivedPrecedences: T12 before T14, T13 before T14, T13 before T19, T13 before T20, T13 before T35. Dropping T13 before T14, T19 and T20 sets aside KICKOFF-EXECUTION-PACKET §4 ('parallel ownership after the kernel stabilizes'), which T14 covers; it depends on ODR-V41-06. Accept them?
options: A: accept the ordering changes
B: keep v4's orderings
requests.recommendation: A, if ODR-V41-06 is A. With v4's estimates, the ordering changes alone shorten the dependency critical path from 340 to 305 minutes and topology C's total from 405 to 395 (schedule.json scenarios). Topology A does not fit the 420-minute window in any scenario; C fits in every scenario.
requests.rationale: The change moves integration risk from T19 to T21 (optimization-report.md, risks R41-02 and R41-03); the owner decides whether that trade is acceptable.
requests.impact: With B, the agent removes the dependency changes from task-adjustments.json and recompiles; the other v4.1 artifacts still apply.

requests.title: Accept the v4.1 estimate changes
requests.question: v4.1 lowers two timed estimates (minutes): T12 25 to 15 and T18 45 to 35. It also gives preflight T10 an estimate of 25 outside the window. Each reason is in analysis/task-adjustments.json; both are the package author's estimates, not measurements. Accept them for planning?
options: A: accept the estimate changes
B: keep v4's estimates
requests.recommendation: A only if the reasons convince you: with v4's orderings, the estimate changes alone take the dependency critical path from 340 to 330 minutes and C from 405 to 395; with ODR-V41-03 also accepted, 300 and 385 (C's makespan 320 plus 65 minutes of reserves).
requests.rationale: Lower estimates move the schedule without moving the work; only the owner accepts them.
requests.impact: With B, the agent restores v4's estimates and recompiles; reserves are unchanged either way.

requests.title: Map UI-016's amber #E9A23B to a Forma token
requests.question: UI-016 (docs/CAUSA-UI-EXPERIENCE-REQUIREMENTS.md) names the identity colour amber #E9A23B and requires every colour to map to a named semantic Forma theme token. Forma 0.12.0 defines no such value (its ambers differ), and v4.1 forbids declaring new --ef-* properties. Which applies?
options: A: use Forma's warning-status token for amber, keeping text labels (DEC-R7-002)
B: allow web/causa.css to declare one theme token for #E9A23B, outside the --ef-* namespace, after measuring contrast
C: ask Forma for a release with the identity colours
requests.recommendation: A for November 7: it uses only published tokens; B or C if the exact hex is required.
requests.rationale: A requirement value and the no-invented-token rule conflict; an agent may not resolve that by itself.
requests.impact: Until decided, FL-06 cites #E9A23B as the requirement's value (check X07 accepts a literal only with its requirement source).

requests.title: Pre-kickoff contracts and scaffolding for November 7
requests.question: Baseline and event clauses conflict with v4.1. (1) docs/REHEARSAL-AGENT-INTERFACE-FREEZE.md preamble and contract-freeze step 1: F# signatures 'MUST be authored from the requirements at kickoff'; 'these are not fabricated compile-ready interfaces'. (2) KICKOFF-EXECUTION-PACKET §4: parallel ownership after the kernel stabilizes. (3) docs/HACKATHON-BOUNDARIES.md, quoting the published event page: 'the repository starts empty' and 'code starts at kickoff'; and its own rules: 'Before producing application-specific executable/generated scaffolding from it before kickoff, confirm organizer interpretation' and 'Until clarified, keep this repository specification-heavy and keep competition application source code out of it.' v4.1 ships compile-ready interface contracts (contracts/), and its bootstrap (T10, before T0) makes the application repository non-empty before kickoff. On 2026-10-30 the owner told the package author in session that the organizers allow pre-kickoff scaffolding. Record that, and set these clauses aside for November 7?
options: A: the organizers allow it; for November 7 the v4.1 contracts are authored before kickoff and committed at T14, and the bootstrap may be generated at T10
B: keep the kickoff-authoring clauses; the contracts become reference text and the bootstrap is not used
requests.recommendation: A, as the owner stated; the owner's own record is what makes it authoritative (the package author may not write it).
requests.rationale: Only the owner can set aside a baseline clause, and only the organizers can interpret the event rules.
requests.impact: With B, T14 returns to authoring at kickoff and ODR-V41-03's waivers of T13 before T14, T19 and T20 fall away.

requests.title: Lock the test tooling
requests.question: requirements-compiled/v4/dependency-lock.json locks no .NET test framework and no Playwright version, yet the plan binds 'dotnet:' and 'playwright:' tests. The bootstrap (v41 --bootstrap) therefore builds the test projects without a test framework, and the layout tests run on the Playwright the CI runner provides. Which test tooling is locked?
options: A: xUnit with Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, and Playwright 1.63.0 (the version this package's layout tests ran on)
B: Expecto, and Playwright 1.63.0
C: another set the owner names
requests.recommendation: A, or whatever Dokimos 0.9.0 documents as its supported runner; the lock entry is added to the dependency lock by the owner's decision, not chosen by an agent.
requests.rationale: Adding a framework needs a verified requirement or an owner decision (v4.1 brief).
requests.impact: Until decided, T10 cannot write the test projects' package references.

requests.title: Amend two v4 state-machine gaps
requests.question: (1) SM-SAVE declares MutationSent, but no transition accepts it, so it fails closed in every state (analysis/guard-partitions.json unusedEvents). (2) SM-LOAD has no transport-failure event; v4.1 routes provider refusals and lost answers through LoadRejected of LoadFailure.ProviderFailed (IF41-SAVE). Amend v4?
options: A: add a Saving + MutationSent transition that records the outstanding request and stays Saving, and accept LoadRejected carrying ProviderFailed for transport failures
B: remove MutationSent from SM-SAVE, and keep SM-LOAD as is
C: leave both as they are
requests.recommendation: A: it changes no state and makes the declared event usable.
requests.rationale: v4.1 may not add transitions or states to v4's machines on its own.
requests.impact: Until decided, MutationSent stays declared and illegal everywhere, so the implementation never emits it.

requests.title: Lock axe-core for the accessibility assertion
requests.question: The event build copies the layout kit (layout-tests/assertions.mjs) as tests/browser/support/layout-assertions.mjs, and its axeClean assertion (FL-06e, bound through PERSIST-030-O6) loads axe-core from the event build's own node_modules. ODR-V41-07 locked the test runners (xUnit, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, @playwright/test) but not axe-core, so T10 cannot add it to package.json. Which axe-core version is locked?
options: A: axe-core 4.14.0 (the version this package's layout tests run with in CI)
B: another version the owner names
requests.recommendation: A: it is the version the layout kit's catch rate and every conforming Forma pattern were measured with; the lock entry is added by the owner's decision, not chosen by an agent.
requests.rationale: Adding a library needs a verified requirement or an owner decision (v4.1 brief). FL-06e requires axe-core checks but names no version.
requests.impact: Until decided, the bootstrap writes no axe-core entry, and the event build's axeClean assertion has no axe-core to load.
